title: What if gravity kept growing?
idea: Fact what-if 02: gravity gets stronger every five seconds (1-5 g, then 5 g steps to 50 g): you black out, then the world breaks through the window, then back to 1 g and the phone loops.

hook.what: you on the sofa, phone over your face, the counter at 1 g and the question on screen; at 1.0 s the phone slams down

props.staged: in his raised right hand, then on his face, then lying on the sofa seat (the cushion is its support)
falling satellites, kilometres up in the sky
falling satellites, kilometres up in the sky
clouds in the sky, then a cloud sea over the street
a black card on the camera lens (tunnel vision)
a black card on the camera lens (the blackout)

captions.text: Every five seconds, gravity gets stronger. In twenty, you black out.
Three g. A rocket launch. Astronauts lie down for this.
Four g. Blood leaves your head. Your eyes go grey.
Five g. Pilots need special suits for this. You don't.
Ten g. Lying flat, blood reaches your head again.
Fifteen. Buildings only hold about twice their weight.
Twenty. The air gets squeezed down. Clouds sink to the street.
Twenty-five. No human survives this. Good thing you're a potato.
Thirty. Every satellite is too slow now. They all fall.
Thirty-five. Air this thick turns oxygen into poison.
Forty. Mountains crush under their own weight.
Forty-five. Even the Moon is falling.
Fifty. It hits in seventeen hours.

visible.why: frame 0: you on the sofa, the phone held over your face; the counter reads 1 g
2 g: the phone slams onto his face
3 g: teeth gritted, pressed into the cushion
5 g: the picture closes to a hole on his face
he has blacked out, slumped back on the sofa
10 g: awake again, pressed flat; the sofa legs splay and the floor cracks
15 g: the glass tower across the street cracks and collapses straight down in dust
20 g: the clouds sink into a sea at street level; tall roofs stick out
25 g: pancake flat, a calm wink on 'Good thing you're a potato'
30 g: every satellite falls, burning trails across the dusk sky
35 g: the air thickens to a haze, he gasps
40 g: on the TV news the Alps slump and avalanche
45 g: the Moon hangs huge and low over the city
50 g: the Moon fills the window, cracking
1 g again: the room is whole, the phone flies back into his hands (the loop)

allowClip.reason: he sits sunk into the sofa: gravity presses him into the cushion (the dip is drawn by the sofa's sink); his widening body spreads into the seat and back cushion
25 g: pancake flat, his rolled collar spreads over his mouth; the wink (the payoff) is in the eyes, which stay clear
the phone lies on his face after the 2 g slam, then slides off
